verdicts.title: An Extension of Khovanov Homology to Immersed Surface Cobordisms
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We show that an oriented surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ containing double point singularities induces a map between the Khovanov homology groups of its boundary links in a functorial way. As part of this work, the movie moves of Carter and Saito are extended to surfaces with double points.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns extending Khovanov homology to immersed surface cobordisms with double points in R^4, which shares only the 'Khovanov homology' vocabulary but says nothing about SAT instances, clause-variable graphs, or resolution proof size.

verdicts.title: Symmetries of equivariant Khovanov homology
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We study symmetries in equivariant versions of Khovanov homology, which include (i) the construction of an involution $\widehatσ$ for the $U(2)$-equivariant theory, (ii) an integral lifting $\widehatν$ of the Shumakovitch operation $ν$, and (iii) splitting of the $U(1)$- and $U(1)\times U(1)$-equivariant theories generalizing earlier work over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Finally, we relate these structures to the Rasmussen $s$-invariant over an arbitrary field $F$.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns symmetries and equivariant structures in Khovanov homology related to the Rasmussen s-invariant ('symmetries in equivariant versions of Khovanov homology'), with no mention of SAT instances, resolution proofs, or clause-variable graphs.

verdicts.title: Geometry and categorification
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We describe a number of geometric contexts where categorification appears naturally: coherent sheaves, constructible sheaves and sheaves of modules over quantizations. In each case, we discuss how "index formulas" allow us to easily perform categorical calculations, and readily relate classical constructions of geometric representation theory to categorical ones.

verdicts.title: Learned Clause Minimization in Parallel SAT Solvers
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Learned clauses minimization (LCM) let to performance improvements of modern SAT solvers especially in solving hard SAT instances. Despite the success of LCM approaches in sequential solvers, they are not widely incorporated in parallel SAT solvers. In this paper we explore the potential of LCM for parallel SAT solvers by defining multiple LCM approaches based on clause vivification, comparing their runtime in different SAT solvers and discussing reasons for performance gains and losses.
